why: E038 showed that only holds of weeks can cover Firi's ~2.5% round trip (needed hit rates: 24 h impossible, 7 d 67-74%, 30 d 57-60%). Every directional experiment so far (E001-E004, E008, E011, E015, E017, E032, E037) sampled HOURLY rows and judged forward horizons of at most 168 h. E004's trend features grew with the horizon in 2018-23 (30-day trailing return: rho +0.07 at 72 h, +0.10 at 168 h) and were flat in 2024-25, and nothing beyond 168 h was ever measured. The positive outside results are daily/weekly time-series momentum and moving-average ratios (Liu & Tsyvinski 2021; Detzel et al. 2021; Moskowitz, Ooi & Pedersen 2012). So the one untested place where a useful directional signal could exist for this trader is multi-week horizons, measured on daily samples with honest effective sample sizes, and judged as a trading rule against random timing with the same turnover.
question: Q1 (map, descriptive): where does BTC's directional structure change sign between reversal and momentum, across lookbacks 1-182 days and horizons 1-30 days? Q2: does any of 14 literature-specified daily signals carry directional information at 1, 7 or 30 days that survives a multiple-testing correction in 2018-23 and keeps its sign in 2024-25? Q3: does fitting them together (one walk-forward logistic) beat the leak-free base rate at 7 days? Q4: does any fixed long/cash rule built on them beat cash after Firi's costs AND random timing with the same turnover, in both periods? Q5 (descriptive): does the trend state change the probability of a large 30-day fall?

E038's C3 is the same 200-day rule as T_MA200 here; it is reproduced as the exactness gate, not re-judged. E005 tested funding against 24 h (a live re-test is registered for about 2027-03-21 on LIVE data; FUND7 here uses development data at 7 days only and does not touch that re-test). E008 tested taker-buy share up to 168 h on hourly rows. New here: forward horizons of 14 and 30 days; daily sampling with explicit effective sample sizes; the 52-week-high ratio, the 50/200 crossover, the equal-weight multi-horizon trend score and its volatility-scaled version; a fitted daily-feature model at 7 days; random-timing nulls for daily trend rules; the conditional probability of a large fall. Not re-run under any name: the category scores (D1), up_streak_6 (D2), the shape group, intraday calibration, macro (E006 void).

hypotheses.H1_map: Short lookbacks (1-3 days) show reversal or nothing; multi-week lookbacks (28-182 days) show momentum at 7-30-day horizons in 2018-23; in 2024-25 the signs are not reliably the same (descriptive).
hypotheses.H2_signals: No signal-horizon pair is REPLICATED (Holm-significant in 2018-23 AND its 2024-25 interval excludes zero with the same sign).
hypotheses.H3_model: The walk-forward logistic does not beat the leak-free base rate at 7 days in 2024-25 with an interval excluding zero.
hypotheses.H4_trading: No trend rule is a TRADING CANDIDATE (the rule below) in both periods; trend rules beat cash in both periods mainly through exposure to a rising market, not through timing.
hypotheses.H5_tail: Below-average-trend states (close under the 200-day average, or a negative trend score) have a higher rate of 30-day falls worse than -20% than the base rate in 2018-23 (descriptive; the protective case for trend following).

expectation_stated_in_advance: Likely: momentum leads at 7-30 days in 2018-23 (the 2019-21 bull market), not confirmed in 2024-25, where the tests are badly under-powered (about 78 independent weeks and 18 independent months); the logistic no better than the base rate; trend rules ahead of cash but not ahead of random timing in 2024-25. A replicated signal would be surprising and is checked hardest. Whatever the outcome, the power table says what the development data can and cannot decide.

research/results/E038/low_frequency.json (committed, d9d4765) for the exactness gate's reference values only.
data.daily_series: The daily close of UTC day d is the close of its 23:00 UTC hourly candle (known at 00:00 UTC of d+1); a day without that candle has no daily close. Daily taker share = sum of the day's taker-buy volume / sum of its volume. Decisions for day d use only information known at the close of day d.
data.boundaries: Statistics and trading from the first UTC day on which every signal except FUND7 exists (FUND7 from its own first valid day) to 2025-06-30. A forward return over H days uses the close of day d+H, so rows whose outcome lies after 2025-06-30 23:00 UTC are excluded by construction (the governed reader stops there) and the code asserts it. Exploration = days before 2024-01-01; validation = 2024-01-01 -> 2025-06-30. Exploration rows whose H-day outcome falls in 2024 are dropped from exploration statistics (no row's outcome crosses the period boundary).
data.never: The sealed holdout (2025-07-01 -> 2026-08-19; research/HOLDOUT_ACCESS.log must still not exist afterwards), the buffer, any live record, the direction shadow track (blind), news, macro (refused snapshot), any download.

signals.R1, R7, R14, R28, R84, R182: past return close_d / close_(d-k) - 1 for k = 1, 7, 14, 28, 84, 182 calendar days (NaN when either close is missing). Time-series momentum lookbacks from the literature (1-4 weeks, 3 and 6 months).
signals.MA20, MA200: close_d / mean(last N available daily closes, today included) - 1, N = 20 and 200 (the 200-day definition is exactly E038's C3).
signals.H52: close_d / max(daily closes over the last 365 calendar days, today included) (George & Hwang's 52-week-high ratio).
signals.TREND: mean of sign(R7), sign(R14), sign(R28), sign(R84), sign(R182): an equal-weight multi-horizon trend score in [-1, 1], no fitting.
signals.TREND_VS: TREND / sigma30, sigma30 = standard deviation of the last 30 daily log returns (volatility-scaled trend; Moskowitz, Ooi & Pedersen 2012).
signals.FUND7: mean of the last 21 funding settlements at or before the day's close (about 7 days); the hypothesis from E005 is contrarian (negative).
signals.TAKER7: taker-buy share of volume over the last 7 days; no sign hypothesis (two-sided).

map: Lookbacks {1, 3, 7, 14, 28, 56, 84, 182} days x horizons {1, 3, 7, 14, 30} days: Spearman rho of the past return with the forward return, both periods, descriptive only (40 cells x 2 periods; no claim is made from a single cell).
prediction_metrics: Per signal x horizon x period: Spearman rho(signal_d, forward H-day return_d) on daily rows; for the sign-type signals (R*, MA*, X50_200, TREND) also the hit rate of sign(signal) against the sign of the forward return; the number of rows and n_eff = rows / H.
power_computed_in_advance: Minimal detectable rho at 80% power, two-sided 5%: 2.80 / sqrt(n_eff). With about 1,960 exploration days and 547 validation days: 1 d: 0.063 / 0.120; 7 d: 0.167 / 0.317; 30 d: 0.35 / 0.66. The 30-day tests, and every validation test beyond 1 day, can only detect large effects; their silence is not evidence of absence.

fitted_model.M7: L2 logistic regression, C = 0.1 (agent.research.model_test.LogisticModel; scaler on training rows only), on the 13 signals other than FUND7, target y = 1 if the 7-day forward return > 0.
fitted_model.walk_forward: Test blocks = calendar years 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023 (exploration) and 2024, 2025 to 06-30 (validation). Training = every eligible day whose 7-day outcome was known 1 day before the block starts (day <= block start - 8 days); at least 365 training rows. One fit per block.
fitted_model.baseline: the leak-free base rate: the UP share of the same training rows (E032's convention).
fitted_model.metric: Brier score and Brier skill = 1 - Brier(M7) / Brier(base) per period; the paired difference Brier(base) - Brier(M7) with a circular block bootstrap of 14-day blocks, 2,000 resamples, seed 31; calibration intercept and slope (descriptive).

trading_rules.decision: once a day on the 23:00 UTC row: fill at that close with cost c per side (E038's arithmetic: a buy of q receives (q - q*c)/close BTC; a sale of x BTC receives x*close - x*close*c); start 150 in cash each period; equity marked at daily closes; long/cash only.
trading_rules.rules: T_R7, T_R14, T_R28, T_R84, T_R182, T_MA20, T_MA200, T_X50_200, T_TREND: fully invested when the signal is > 0, otherwise cash. T_TREND_VS: exposure = min(1, max(0, TREND) * 0.0294 / sigma30) (0.0294 = rule-1.0's 0.6% an hour as a daily figure), rebalanced only when the change exceeds 20% of equity, or to exit or enter fully. T_M7: invested when M7's p > 0.5, on M7's out-of-sample days only.
trading_rules.benchmarks: buy-and-hold (one entry), cash, and exposure-matched buy-and-hold (a constant exposure equal to the rule's mean exposure, no costs; descriptive).
trading_rules.metrics: final equity, net and annualised return, mean daily return with a 95% interval (20-day blocks, 2,000, seed 31), paired daily difference against buy-and-hold, Sharpe (sqrt 365), maximum drawdown, actions and cycles per year, mean exposure, mean holding days, costs paid, per calendar year.
trading_rules.random_timing_null: the rule's daily target-exposure path circularly shifted against the daily returns by 200 offsets drawn uniformly from [60, N - 60] days (seed 2039), simulated at S0 and at S3 (same turnover, random timing); the actual result's percentile among the 200.

tail_table: Descriptive: the share of days whose 30-day forward return is below -20%, and the mean 30-day forward return, overall and by MA200 state (above / below) and by TREND value (-1 ... +1), per period, with 60-day-block bootstrap intervals (2,000, seed 31).
uncertainty: Circular block bootstrap (agent.research.metrics.block_bootstrap_estimates); block = max(2H, 14) days for H-day statistics; 2,000 resamples; seed 31; percentile 95% intervals; two-sided bootstrap p = min(1, 2 * min(1 + #{x* <= 0}, 1 + #{x* >= 0}) / (1 + 2,000)) (E036's formula).
multiple_comparisons: The signal family is 14 signals x 3 horizons = 42 exploration tests, Holm-adjusted at family-wise 0.05. The map (40 cells) is descriptive and never used to select. Trading: 10 fixed rules plus T_M7; with 11 rules about one in twenty reaches the 95th null percentile in one period by chance, about one in four hundred in both, so 'both periods' is required.

what_each_answer_means_decided_in_advanc.signal: LEAD: Holm-adjusted exploration p < 0.05 AND the validation point estimate has the same sign. REPLICATED: a LEAD whose validation 95% interval also excludes zero with that sign. NO EVIDENCE otherwise. A REPLICATED pair is a candidate for a separately registered PROSPECTIVE daily direction track (the owner's decision); a LEAD alone is only a hypothesis.
what_each_answer_means_decided_in_advanc.model: SUPPORTED: validation Brier(base) - Brier(M7) > 0 with its interval above zero AND the exploration point estimate > 0. NOT_SUPPORTED: the validation interval lies below zero, or the exploration estimate <= 0. INCONCLUSIVE otherwise.
what_each_answer_means_decided_in_advanc.trading: A rule is a TRADING CANDIDATE only if, in BOTH periods: its S3 mean daily return has a 95% interval above zero; its S4 point estimate is above zero; its S0 result is at or above the 95th percentile of its random-timing null; it completes at least 8 cycles. Otherwise NOT SUPPORTED. A candidate authorises nothing: the next step would be its own registration and a prospective record, with the owner's approval.
what_each_answer_means_decided_in_advanc.tail: Descriptive. A state whose rate of large falls differs from the base rate with intervals excluding it in BOTH periods, same direction, is reported as a lead for risk control (not for direction).

compute_and_storage: Local only, a few minutes: no network, no AI call, no database, no new table, no workflow, no paid service. Output under research/results/E039/ (JSON + markdown, < 5 MB).
execution_details_fixed_before_any_resul: Side data comes only through the one reviewed route, agent.research.feature_test.compute_group_features (research/HOLDOUT_ROUTES.md), cut at the candles' own information cutoff; tests/test_holdout_routes.py stays unchanged. Its features are taken at each day's 23:00 UTC row.
FUND7 = that route's funding_sum_21 / 21: the mean of the last 21 settlements at or before the day's close, exactly as registered.

TAKER7 = the mean of the last 7 daily values of that route's taker_buy_share_24h (equal weight per day). The record said 'taker-buy share of volume over the last 7 days'; the route gives the 24 h share, not the volumes, so this is the equal-weighted version. Decided before any result.
sigma30 = the standard deviation of the daily log returns over the last 30 calendar days, needing at least 20 of them (missing days leave gaps).

The trading rules T_MA20 / T_MA200 compare close > SMA directly (E038's own comparison, needed for the exactness gate); the MA20 / MA200 signal values are the ratios. Every SMA is sum(last N available daily closes) / N, as in E038.

A day without a daily close, or with its signal missing, is no decision: the position is kept. T_M7 trades from M7's first out-of-sample day (2020-01-01) to the period's end, and its buy-and-hold comparison uses the same days.
result: Daily rows 2,874 (2017-08-17 -> 2025-06-30, one missing day); study from 2018-08-16; FUND7 from 2019-09-16. Exactness gate: 10 of 10 (T_MA200 = E038's C3 at five costs, both periods), largest difference 0.0. No tripwire. MAP (Spearman, past L-day vs forward H-day return): exploration shows the 1-day reversal (L1/H1 -0.074 [-0.121, -0.025]) and momentum from 28-56-day lookbacks at 3-14-day horizons (L28: H3 +0.070, H7 +0.100, H14 +0.135, intervals above zero; H30 +0.182 [-0.023, +0.347]); validation shows no momentum and REVERSAL at long lookbacks (L182/H3 -0.121 and L182/H30 -0.420 [-0.687, -0.127], L84/H30 -0.163). SIGNALS: smallest Holm-adjusted p 0.294 (R1/F1, the 1-day reversal: -0.074 / -0.064 [-0.142, +0.014]); every other >= 0.99. MODEL M7 (7 days): exploration Brier 0.2802 vs base 0.2528, base - M7 = -0.0274 [-0.0430, -0.0117] (worse than the base rate), calibration slope -0.19; validation 0.2468 vs 0.2471, +0.0003 [-0.0075, +0.0074], slope 0.44: NOT_SUPPORTED. Its trading rule was below random timing in 2020-23 (6th percentile, gross -32%) and above it in 2024-25 (100th, gross +295%): a sign flip, not skill. TRADING at S3 (1.25% a side), exploration / validation net: X50_200 +366% / +41%; MA200 +351% / +21%; R84 +151% / +58%; R182 +87% / +103%; R28 +214% / -32%; TREND +9% / -33%; TREND_VS +27% / -14%; R14 -31% / -21%; MA20 -71% / -18%; R7 -95% / -61%; M7 -90% / +36%; buy-and-hold +570% / +142.5%. Random-timing null (S0 percentile), exploration / validation: R14 99.5 / 74; R28 100 / 29.5; TREND 99 / 36.5; TREND_VS 100 / 76; MA200 92 / 14.5; X50_200 85 / 20.5; R84 92 / 61; R182 71.5 / 31; M7 6 / 100. No rule meets the candidate rule in both periods. Maximum drawdowns of the low-turnover rules at S3 in 2018-23: 68%-79% (buy-and-hold about 77%, E038). TAIL (30-day falls worse than -20%): exploration 10.1% of days; above / below the 200-day 9.8% / 10.4%; TREND +1.0 5.5% [0.7%, 12.1%] vs -0.6 15.7% [4.7%, 28.8%] (overlapping); validation 1 such day in 517 (untestable). Reading: across 1 h to 30 days the only directional structure with the same sign in both periods is the short reversal, far below costs; multi-week trend is a regime property (momentum 2018-23, reversal 2024-25), not a stable predictor; fitting the signals together is worse than the base rate.
